summary: 1942 Missouri Conservation lookout near Camdenton, built with steel from a former Eldon water tower; standing, and MDC says visitors can walk up it.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower; its steel came from a former Eldon city water tower

access.note: MDC says visitors can walk up the tower. The area is open to public use only as authorized by posting, with special hours.

visit.trail_note: The 45 mostly-wooded acres include an archery range, hiking trail and an ADA-accessible trail section beside the Conservation Service Center office.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and the Forest Lookouts page describe a 60-foot tower; the current MDC site page says 80 feet. The record keeps 60 feet (18.3 m) for the tower built in 1942, and the story reports the MDC figure as a conflict.
A 1941 newspaper quote says the tower was being completed; the 1942 Commission report says it was completed. The Register gives 1942. The record uses 1942.

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: 60 feet (Register, Forest Lookouts) vs 80 feet (MDC current page). The story flags it and keeps 60 feet. The MDC page is undated, so the 'standing' and public-access status reflects what it said when fetched on 2026-10-09. The brief's 'standing' is now supported by MDC. A 2018 MDC Central Region towersites plan PDF mentions the Camdenton towersite; I saw it only in a search snippet and did not read it. It may settle the height and condition. Staffing today is not stated by any source; the towerman quote is a 1941 plan. No rental listing found. No photos added.
